findings.title: No runtime array guard — the module's "never throw" property is conditional on the caller
findings.description: findSwapIndex calls order.indexOf(...), order.length, order[i] and hiddenGroups.includes(...) with no shape check. The declared parameter type GroupId[] is erased at build time, so a non-array value coming from a hand-edited data.json propagates straight into these calls. Verified by direct probe of the compiled module: order = null / undefined / {} and hiddenGroups = null / undefined / {} each raise an uncaught TypeError (e.g. "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'indexOf')", "hiddenGroups.includes is not a function"). Task 04, step 4 states the requirement more broadly than the acceptance criteria do — "Keep the functions total and defensive: never throw" — and that broader property does not hold. Reachability today is limited and is the reason this is minor, not major: board.groupOrder is re-sanitized on every load by sanitizeGroupOrder (src/data/migration.ts:152-157, outside every version branch), so `order` is always a clean permutation of the six ids; and Task 08 feeds the arrows a local array built by spreading board.hiddenGroups, which itself throws earlier for a null value. The module is therefore a second failure site, not the first one — but it is the only layer that could still make the settings popup fail on an already-open board, and the guard costs three lines. A second, quieter symptom of the same missing check: a string hiddenGroups does not throw at all — `.includes` silently switches to substring semantics, so "focusBar".includes("focus") reports a group hidden when it is not, and arrows behave incorrectly without any visible error.
findings.location: src/ui/groupOrderUtils.ts:23-36 (findSwapIndex — order.indexOf at :23, hiddenGroups.includes at :26 and :34)
findings.impact: An uncaught TypeError inside a Svelte click handler on hand-corrupted data.json. In the settings popup this leaves the dialog in a half-rendered state with no user-facing message; the exception surfaces only in the developer console. No data loss (moveGroup never mutates its inputs) and no privilege or confidentiality consequence — this is availability of one dialog on locally corrupted data.

findings.title: hiddenGroups is never sanitized, so the invariant this module relies on is not enforced anywhere
findings.description: Adjacent-scope finding, raised because it is what makes finding 1 reachable at all. The feature sanitizes groupOrder and group titles on every load (src/data/migration.ts:152-157, deliberately outside the version branches, per tech-spec Decision 6), but hiddenGroups gets no equivalent treatment. The only code that ever touches it is the version < 4 branch (src/data/migration.ts:100-105), which (a) replaces the value only when it is strictly `undefined` — `null`, a string, or an object all pass through — and (b) does not run at all for data already at version 4 or above, which is every current install. Decision 6's own rationale ("Handling only the array case would still throw on a hand-edited null — the very outcome this is meant to prevent") applies verbatim to hiddenGroups, but the decision was scoped to groupOrder only. Concrete consequence with `"hiddenGroups": null` in a v8 data.json: the board itself still renders (BoardLayout.svelte:21 uses `new Set(board.hiddenGroups)`, and `new Set(null)` is legal and yields an empty set), but opening board settings throws at BoardSettingsPopup.svelte:14 `[...board.hiddenGroups]`. With `"hiddenGroups": {}` the spread throws as well. That failure predates this commit; what is new is that Task 08 will route the same unvalidated value into groupOrderUtils.
findings.location: src/data/migration.ts:100-105 and :152-157 (asymmetry with sanitizeGroupOrder); consumed at src/ui/groupOrderUtils.ts:26
findings.impact: Board settings become unreachable on a hand-corrupted or externally-synced data.json, with no message and no self-repair — the same class of failure Decision 6 was written to eliminate for groupOrder. Local availability only; no confidentiality or integrity impact.
